back: Species with an unpaired electron; highly reactive.
Bond breaks with one electron to each atom, forming two radicals (UV/heat).
Initiation (make radicals), propagation (radical in, radical out), termination (two radicals combine).
CH₄ + Cl• → CH₃• + HCl; CH₃• + Cl₂ → CH₃Cl + Cl•.

front: Initiation step for chlorination of methane?
back: Cl₂ → 2Cl• — homolytic fission of the weakest bond by UV light.
Cl• + Cl• → Cl₂; CH₃• + Cl• → CH₃Cl; CH₃• + CH₃• → C₂H₆ (ethane is evidence for the mechanism).
UV light (sunlight) or high temperature, to break the X–X bond homolytically. No reaction in the dark at room temperature.

front: Overall equation for monochlorination of methane?
Why does radical substitution give a mixture of products?
back: Cl• can abstract H from chloromethane too, giving CH₂Cl₂, CHCl₃ and CCl₄; termination also forms longer chains. Excess alkane favours monosubstitution.
Strong, non-polar C–C and C–H bonds (similar electronegativities), so no δ+/δ− sites to attract nucleophiles or electrophiles.

front: How is the movement of a single electron shown?
back: A single-headed (fish-hook) arrow; the radical’s unpaired electron is shown as a dot (Cl•).

front: Why is it called a chain reaction?
back: Each propagation step uses one radical and regenerates another, so one initiation can lead to thousands of propagation cycles.

front: Why does UV break Cl–Cl rather than C–H?
back: Cl–Cl (242 kJ mol⁻¹) is much weaker than C–H (414 kJ mol⁻¹); UV photons have enough energy only for Cl–Cl.

front: Bromination of ethane: overall equation and observation?
back: C₂H₆ + Br₂ → C₂H₅Br + HBr (UV); orange-brown bromine colour fades slowly.
No. Radicals are usually neutral (Cl•, CH₃•) — they have an unpaired electron, not a charge (unlike ions from heterolytic fission).
An atom in the alkane (H) is replaced by another atom (Cl or Br); the carbon skeleton is unchanged.

front: Why is the methyl radical CH₃• reactive?
back: C has only seven valence electrons (three bonding pairs + one unpaired electron); it reacts to pair the electron and complete its octet.
Homolytic: one electron to each atom → two radicals (UV, non-polar bonds). Heterolytic: both electrons to one atom → a cation and an anion (polar bonds).

front: Propagation steps for chlorination of ethane?
back: C₂H₆ + Cl• → C₂H₅• + HCl; C₂H₅• + Cl₂ → C₂H₅Cl + Cl•.
